The information in the figure shows that these proteins affect the expression of FRSL, and the question stem also states that BLD and DRKFR have an interaction. Then reason: the question asks "why these proteins are able to bind to each other," which belongs to the mechanism of physical protein binding, not the issue of expression level. Protein-protein binding usually depends on matching of three-dimensional structural surfaces, especially binding sites with complementary shapes and chemical properties. The most likely structural feature is amino acid pockets/interfaces that can fit into each other, that is, amino acid pockets with complementary conformations.
